This review companion follows the headings in **Table discussion.pdf** (seven
pages, supplied November 10, 2026). It is kept under `design/`, which is excluded
from the package. The package vignette **Reporting simulation results** explains
the APIs and assumptions in workflow order.

These examples reproduce the available reporting layouts with newly simulated
illustrative results, rather than the sponsors' original numerical results or
visual styling. HTML output uses gt when installed, including native column
spanners and row sections. Bayer's six true-probability rows match the notes; dose amounts
and the design are illustrative. BI examples here use one arm. Missing features
are flagged beside the corresponding example for a separate implementation step.

To render from the repository root (requires `devtools` and Quarto):

```r
 quarto::quarto_render("design/966-table-reporting/table-discussion-review.qmd")
```

The review setup loads the development package from this checkout.
The document reads the vignette source chunks so that both documents execute the
same examples. It does not depend on the private PDF file or its Desktop path.

```{r review-init, include=FALSE}
devtools::load_all("../..", quiet = TRUE)
source_path <- "../../vignettes/reporting-simulation-results.Rmd.orig"
code_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")
knitr::purl(source_path, output = code_path, documentation = 1, quiet = TRUE)
knitr::read_chunk(code_path)
unlink(code_path)
```

```{r reporting-setup, include=FALSE}
```

```{r review-figures, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = "table-discussion-review-figures/")
```

```{r reporting-design}
```

```{r reporting-prior-samples, include=FALSE}
```

# Bayer

## Prior definition plot

PDF p. 2: mean and 95% prior credible interval with optional target overlay.

```{r reporting-prior-plot}
```

## Prior random draws plot

PDF p. 2: 100 curves drawn from the same prior samples.

```{r reporting-prior-draws}
```

## Scenario definition table

PDF pp. 2–3, Table 10-3: the six probability rows are transcribed from the notes.

```{r reporting-truth-table}
```

## Scenario definition plot

PDF p. 3, Figure 10-1: the same probabilities, with the study's target band.

```{r reporting-truth-plot}
```

## Operating characteristics table

PDF pp. 3–4: native row sections, supplied stopping-rule labels, selections, correct selections, sample-size
summaries, patients above target, and per-dose patients/DLTs. Per-dose SDs are
shown using the requested mean (SD) option.

```{r reporting-bayer}
```

Additional available customization: above-target min/max and quantiles via
`OCStat`, using the cached summary.

```{r reporting-custom}
```

**Flagged for later:** the special "highest planned dose safe" outcome needs a
rule-based definition and is not a synonym for highest-dose selection. Duration
mean/SD exists for `DASimulations` with recorded durations; this example has no
elapsed time. Cohort-scaled duration and duration min/max/quantiles are not
provided by the current registry. The notes' five particular stop reasons also
require a design containing those rules; this example has toxicity, no-admissible-dose, and
maximum-size rules. Above-target distribution summaries use custom
statistics rather than built-in min/max and quantile entries.

## Plots

PDF pp. 4–5: selection percentages and patient counts.

```{r reporting-selection-plot}
```

```{r reporting-patients-plot}
```

The PDF's per-dose patient-count boxplots and violin
plots are shown below through `plot_type`. The PDF's BOIN comparison and
true-rate annotation strip are not reproduced by these CRM reporting plots.

```{r reporting-patient-distributions}
```

**Flagged for later:** a native comparison across different designs and a
true-rate annotation strip for these plots.

# Boehringer

## Summary of Prior Table

PDF pp. 5–6, Tables 9–10: interval probabilities, mean, SD and quantiles.
Columns follow the PDF order: interval probabilities, mean, SD, quantiles.
The interval and quantile columns have native gt spanners.
Here intervals match the illustrative study's 20–35% target; the PDF uses
16–33%. This is a single-arm prior table.

```{r reporting-prior-table}
```

**Flagged for later:** one native multi-arm/combination prior table matching
both screenshots is not supported by `report_prob_summary()`.

## Hypothetical Data Scenarios aka Trial Realizations Table

PDF p. 6, Table 13: actual `scenario()` evaluations of three trial snapshots.
The last snapshot illustrates a stopping decision.

```{r reporting-data-table}
```

The reporter supports combination and hierarchical `DataScenario` objects,
including arm names. Native spanners group observed data and proposed-dose
interval probabilities. `NextBestNCRM` now calculates underdose probability
from the same posterior draws, so all three interval probabilities are shown.
**Flagged for later:** the exact two-arm scenario from the notes.

## Scenario Definition Table

PDF p. 6, Table 14: single-agent counterpart using the shared six true scenarios.

```{r review-bi-truth-table}
report_table(truths, format = report_format, digits = 3)
```

**Flagged for later:** arm-specific and combination true-toxicity grids are
not supported by `ToxicityScenarios`.

## Operating characteristics Table

PDF p. 6, Table 15: selection classifications, no recommendation, mean and
min/max sample sizes and DLT counts.

```{r reporting-bi}
```

**Flagged for later:** hierarchical OC arm subcolumns and paired mean
(min–max) cells. `report_transpose()` now places scenarios in rows, with
separate mean and range columns. No-recommendation
percentage is computed directly, rather than by adding overlapping stop rules.

# Merck

## Operating characteristics overview table

PDF pp. 6–7: six PMDA-style metrics. The joint maximum-size/no-recommendation
statistic uses the public `OCStat` extension interface to match the row meaning.
The built-in maximum-size stopping percentage alone would also count trials
with an MTD recommendation.

```{r reporting-pmda}
```

## Operating characteristics detail table

PDF p. 7: dose columns, scenario groups, counts, selection, true P(DLT), and
SUM/STOP/MAX. SUM uses per-trial totals for count rows. STOP/MAX count terminal
rule activations, can overlap with recommendations, and need not make the row
sum to 100%. This is the current API's meaning, which reviewers should assess
against their desired reporting convention.

```{r reporting-merck}
```

# Additional reporting capabilities

These additions go beyond the screenshot layouts: reversible transposition,
unrounded cell inspection,
automatic column pagination, markdown rendering, and optional gt/Word export.
See the package vignette for export prerequisites.

```{r reporting-transpose}
```
